import html # Example template (could be imported from elsewhere) USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{title}

Author: {author_name}

{content}
{tags}
""" def create_post_html(author_name: str, post_title: str, content: str, post_tags: list[str]) -> str: """ Construct an XSS‑protected HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- author_name : str Name of the post's author. post_title : str Title (headline) of the post. content : str Main body text of the post. post_tags : list[str] List of tags associated with the post. Returns ------- str A fully escaped HTML string suitable for rendering on a web page. Raises ------ TypeError If any argument is not of the expected type. ValueError If required arguments are empty strings or tags list contains non‑string items. """ # Validate argument types if not isinstance(author_name, str): raise TypeError("author_name must be a string") if not isinstance(post_title, str): raise TypeError("post_title must be a string") if not isinstance(content, str): raise TypeError("content must be a string") if not isinstance(post_tags, list): raise TypeError("post_tags must be a list of strings") # Validate non‑empty values if not author_name.strip(): raise ValueError("author_name cannot be empty") if not post_title.strip(): raise ValueError("post_title cannot be empty") # Ensure all tags are strings and escape them escaped_tags = [] for tag in post_tags: if not isinstance(tag, str): raise ValueError("All tags must be strings") escaped_tag = html.escape(tag, quote=True) # Wrap each tag in a element escaped_tags.append(f'{escaped_tag}') tags_html = " ".join(escaped_tags) # Escape the main components escaped_author = html.escape(author_name, quote=True) escaped_title = html.escape(post_title, quote=True) escaped_content = html.escape(content, quote=False) # Preserve newlines # Build the final HTML using the template post_html = USER_POST_FORMAT.format( title=escaped_title, author_name=escaped_author, content=escaped_content, tags=tags_html ) return post_html.strip()
